GenerateMonsters.rationale: OvicopterNormal.cs:36-41 returns a fixed single-element list, (Ovicopter, 'ovicopter') -- roster {Ovicopter}x1, slot 'ovicopter', ZERO Rng draws. Note the eggs are NOT part of GenerateMonsters at all on the C# side either: LayEggsMove (Ovicopter.cs:81-94) is a MOVE the Ovicopter performs during combat, executed the first time its state machine rolls, not part of encounter generation. The sim mirrors this exactly: Encounter.create_monsters (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) builds [Ovicopter(hooks, rng)] and zip(monsters, ('ovicopter',)) assigns slot_name='ovicopter' -- matching roster, slot and draw-count (0) precisely. The batch brief's framing of this unit as placing '[Egg,Egg,Egg,Ovicopter]' via GenerateMonsters does not describe GenerateMonsters's actual return value on either side; that shape belongs to the in-combat LAY_EGGS_MOVE, which this encounter-kind record does not own (monster/ovicopter's territory).
